bull.argument: The filing shows a business with strong current scale and profitability. Total 2025 revenue was $200.97 billion, up 22% year-over-year, and income from operations rose 20% to $83.28 billion. Family of Apps delivered a 52% operating margin on $198.76 billion of revenue. Ad impressions grew 12% and average price per ad rose 9%, meaning growth came from both more ads delivered and higher monetization per ad. Family daily active people reached 3.58 billion, up 7%, giving the advertising engine a very large base. The company also returned capital, with $26.26 billion in share repurchases and $5.32 billion in dividends, while holding $81.59 billion in cash and marketable securities. The filing acknowledges real headwinds: regulatory limits on ad targeting, Apple and Google changes, and Reels monetizing at a lower rate. Yet management reports that its AI-driven ad and engagement improvements are already improving results for advertisers. The Reality Labs losses of $19.19 billion are large but are funded by a core business whose cash generation, as the filing describes, supports them.

claims.claim: Revenue grew 22% year-over-year to $200.97 billion, driven by advertising.
claims.quote: Total revenue for 2025 was $200.97 billion, an increase of 22% compared to 2024, due to an increase in advertising revenue.

claims.claim: Growth came from both more ad impressions and higher pricing per ad.
claims.quote: Ad impressions delivered across our Family of Apps in 2025 increased 12% year-over-year, and our average price per ad increased 9% year-over-year.

claims.claim: Management reports its AI-driven ad improvements are already improving advertiser results.
claims.quote: We believe our ongoing improvements to ad targeting and measurement are continuing to drive improved results for advertisers.

bear.argument: The filing's headline strength masks several risks the bear case must weigh. Nearly all revenue comes from advertising on Facebook and Instagram, and marketers have no long-term commitments: 'our marketers do not have long-term advertising commitments with us.' Ad targeting is being eroded by regulation and platform changes, and management concedes these 'will continue to adversely impact our advertising revenue for the foreseeable future.' Growth is also increasingly reliant on price: average price per ad rose 9% while impressions rose 12%, and Reels 'monetizes at a lower rate' than Feed and Stories, with that expected to persist. Spending is heavy and rising: capital expenditures reached $72.22 billion, and management expects AI 'will require significantly increased investment in infrastructure.' Reality Labs cut operating profit by $19.19 billion and losses are expected to 'remain similar' in 2026. Finally, the effective tax rate rose to 30%, and management admits it cannot 'quantify the exact impact' of each trend on revenue. Strong results today do not guarantee these pressures will not compound.

claims.claim: Marketers have no long-term commitment, so revenue can fall quickly if spending shifts.
claims.quote: our marketers do not have long-term advertising commitments with us

claims.claim: Management expects regulatory and platform changes to keep hurting ad revenue.
claims.quote: the legislative, regulatory and platform developments described above will continue to adversely impact our advertising revenue for the foreseeable future

claims.claim: Reality Labs losses are large and expected to continue at a similar level.
claims.quote: we expect our 2026 RL operating losses to remain similar to 2025

bull.argument: The bear case is right that risks are real, but several of its points cut less deeply than presented. On marketers, the filing says the lack of long-term commitments is 'common in the industry,' yet revenue still grew 22% and ad impressions rose 12%, showing demand is broad rather than fragile. On targeting, management says its improvements 'are continuing to drive improved results for advertisers,' so the headwind is being actively offset. On pricing, a 9% rise in average price per ad alongside 12% more impressions indicates that monetization is improving across the base, not simply extracted from a shrinking audience. Reels' lower monetization is a mix effect that management is working to close. On spending, capex of $72.22 billion is funded by a business with a 52% Family of Apps operating margin and $81.59 billion in cash and securities, and the filing ties Reality Labs losses to that core profit. The 30% tax rate includes a one-time valuation allowance charge; excluding it, the rate would have been 13%. The bear's strongest point is that these pressures may compound, and I concede that is a genuine risk to monitor.

claims.claim: Revenue grew 22% despite the acknowledged marketer and targeting risks.
claims.quote: Total revenue for 2025 was $200.97 billion, an increase of 22% compared to 2024, due to an increase in advertising revenue.

claims.claim: Management says its ad targeting improvements are already improving advertiser results.
claims.quote: We believe our ongoing improvements to ad targeting and measurement are continuing to drive improved results for advertisers.

claims.claim: The 30% tax rate was inflated by a one-time charge; excluding it, the rate would have been 13%.
claims.quote: Absent the valuation allowance charge as of the enactment date, our 2025 effective tax rate would have decreased by 17 percentage points to 13%.

bear.argument: The opponent's rebuttal is fair on several points, but the filing does not support their conclusions as strongly as they claim. Strong growth today does not erase forward risk. On targeting, management says its improvements are 'continuing to drive improved results for advertisers,' yet in the same passage it expects regulatory and platform developments to keep hurting ad revenue 'for the foreseeable future,' and it adds that some efforts 'will be long-term initiatives.' Offsetting a headwind over the long term is not the same as eliminating it. On price, the filing says ad impressions grew 12% and average price per ad rose 9%, but it also says that Reels 'monetizes at a lower rate' and 'we expect it will continue to monetize at a lower rate for the foreseeable future,' so mix is a drag, not merely a temporary gap. On the tax rate, excluding the valuation allowance charge the rate would have been 13%, but that charge is still a real cost in 2025. Reality Labs is not a rounding error: it cut operating profit by $19.19 billion, and its losses are expected to remain similar in 2026. The opponent concedes compounding risk, and that concession is the core of this case.

claims.claim: Management expects regulatory and platform headwinds to persist, even as it describes improvements.
claims.quote: the legislative, regulatory and platform developments described above will continue to adversely impact our advertising revenue for the foreseeable future

claims.claim: Reels monetizes at a lower rate and management expects that to continue, so the mix drag is not simply temporary.
claims.quote: we expect it will continue to monetize at a lower rate for the foreseeable future

claims.claim: Reality Labs losses are large and expected to stay similar in 2026, relying on core profits to fund them.
claims.quote: we expect our 2026 RL operating losses to remain similar to 2025

judge.reasoning: Both sides cite verified quotes accurately from the filing, so evidence quality is roughly even. The bull effectively rebuts the bear's marketer-commitment and tax-rate points, showing that the 13% ex-charge rate and continued revenue growth blunt several risks, but it does not directly address the forward-looking 'foreseeable future' headwind language. The bear responds well by pinning the bull to management's own admission that headwinds persist and that Reels monetization lag is structural, though its treatment of the tax charge as a real ongoing cost is somewhat weaker; the result is a close debate.
